title: TikTok Shop Targets 13.2% Share Across Southeast Asia E-Commerce - Retail News Asia

 Why it matters
 TikTok Shop targets a US$15 billion gross merchandise value in Southeast Asia this year, capturing an estimated 13.2 per cent regional e-commerce market share. 
 Surging livestream sales directly threaten Tokopedia and Lazada while forcing market leader Shopee to divert resources to defend engagement formats against video-led buying. 
 Upcoming full-year market data from Momentum Works will reveal whether TikTok Shop can successfully expand past beauty baskets into higher-value categories. 
 Retail News Asia newsroom analysis
 TikTok Shop is projected to take a 13.2 per cent share of Southeast Asia’s e-commerce market in 2023, upending the hierarchy established by regional incumbents. The platform is tracking toward a gross merchandise value target of US$15 billion this year, according to data from venture builder Momentum Works.
 That volume represents more than a threefold jump from the US$4.4 billion recorded across the region in 2022. The rapid expansion pulls the ByteDance unit into direct parity with Indonesian market leader Tokopedia, which holds an estimated 13.9 per cent share, while closing the gap on Lazada at 17.7 per cent.
 Beauty Baskets Drive Volume Growth
 Personal care and beauty products form the engine of the platform’s regional expansion. The category accounts for 84 per cent of all products sold on TikTok Shop and generates 70 per cent of its total gross merchandise value.
 Merchants and cosmetics brands rely heavily on product bundling strategies across their livestreams to push average order values higher. By pairing skin creams, lip tints and cleansers into discounted kits, sellers generate bulk purchases from viewers watching real-time product demonstrations.
 The concentration in beauty mirrors the early development of social commerce in mainland China, where low-ticket impulse buys established initial buying habits before consumers shifted toward consumer electronics and household goods.
 Shopee Steps Up Indonesian Livestream Battle
 Market leader Shopee still retains the dominant regional footprint with a projected 46.5 per cent market share for 2023. Sea Group is responding directly by diverting resources into its own live shopping features to defend its merchant base in major markets like Indonesia.
 “ Market leader Shopee still retains the dominant regional footprint with a projected 46.5 per cent market share for 2023. ” 
 During its 7.7 campaign in Indonesia, Shopee logged a 12-fold increase in transaction volumes through livestreaming channels compared to a standard trading day, Sea Group chief executive Forrest Li told analysts on an earnings call. That spending shift demonstrates how legacy marketplace operators must now pay to defend engagement formats they once treated as optional add-ons.
 For consumer brands and multi-channel retailers across Southeast Asia, the fragmentation of platform market share alters commercial use. Sellers no longer rely entirely on Shopee search placements or Lazada campaign days to clear inventory. Instead, marketing budgets are flowing toward video creator networks, changing merchant acquisition costs and logistics routing across Jakarta.
 Disruption Tests Traditional Network Effects
 Established marketplaces long operated under the assumption that vast merchant catalogs and established logistics routes created insurmountable defenses. The surge of video-led buying breaks that pattern by pulling purchasing directly into entertainment feeds.
 “The bigger narrative is that in ecommerce, where leading players seem to have a network effect and structural advantage, disruption can still happen, and the incumbents should always remain focused and vigilant,” Chen said in a statement.
 Weihan Chen, insights lead at Momentum Works, noted that incumbents face structural pressure regardless of whether TikTok Shop operates as an isolated social platform or a full-scale marketplace operator.
 The threat is particularly sharp in Indonesia, Southeast Asia’s biggest retail economy, where ByteDance has staged extensive offline merchant recruitment drives and creator summits. Having reached scale in beauty, the platform now faces the harder operational test of building delivery networks and merchant infrastructure capable of handling bulkier, higher-value consumer goods without margin erosion.
 Momentum Works is scheduled to release the complete market share dataset across Southeast Asia’s digital commerce sector in an upcoming research report, outlining full-year regional gross merchandise volume tallies.

 ByteDance’s aggressive push will succeed in destabilising incumbents Tokopedia and Lazada, but sustaining momentum requires high operational execution. By relying on livestreamed cosmetics bundles, TikTok Shop mirrors early social commerce in mainland China, yet that heavy beauty bias creates vulnerability. Rival Shopee is already defending its territory effectively, using events like its 7.7 campaign to generate huge livestream transaction spikes. The primary commercial risk lies in logistics, as shifting from low-ticket beauty impulse buys to bulkier consumer electronics threatens margins. Track whether ByteDance hits its US$15 billion gross merchandise value target when Momentum Works publishes its full-year regional dataset.
 Sarah Chen
 Questions & Answers
 Q. What is driving the bulk of TikTok Shop's sales in Southeast Asia?
 A. Personal care and beauty products drive the platform's regional growth, representing 84 per cent of items sold and 70 per cent of gross merchandise value. Merchants rely on livestream product bundling, pairing cosmetics and skincare into discounted kits to increase order values.
 Q. How does TikTok Shop’s projected market share compare with existing regional platforms?
 A. TikTok Shop is forecast to capture 13.2 per cent of Southeast Asia's e-commerce market in 2023. This puts the platform near parity with Tokopedia's 13.9 per cent share and narrows the gap with Lazada at 17.7 per cent, though Shopee maintains a dominant 46.5 per cent share.
 Q. How are incumbent platforms such as Shopee defending their market positions?
 A. Market leader Shopee is diverting resources into its own live shopping tools to protect its merchant base. During a 7.7 campaign in Indonesia, the platform recorded a 12-fold increase in livestream transaction volumes compared with a standard trading day.
 Q. What key operational hurdle must TikTok Shop overcome as it expands further?
 A. After reaching scale in beauty, the platform must construct delivery networks and merchant infrastructure capable of handling bulkier, higher-value consumer goods. Managing these larger shipments without eroding profit margins represents its most demanding logistical test across the region.
